beats.trigger: ## From Personal to Team
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: You can't really share an agent.
beats.got: Sharing is about context, skills, output or interface, and the hard part is whether people take it up.

beats.trigger: Walk in with one example where people had access to a tool or process but real use did not follow.
beats.got: I should think of a time a tool was rolled out and nobody used it. Our dispatch-pricing dashboard is an example.

beats.trigger: **Select** the smallest shareable form (share context / share a skill / share the output / share an interface) for the outcome the teammate wants moved
beats.got: A list of five verbs. The 'smallest shareable form' idea is useful.

beats.trigger: who's the one person who came to mind just now?
beats.got: I thought of Mikael on my pricing working group, and I hesitate because he'd get a generic answer from it.

beats.trigger: Your teammate doesn't want your agent. They want a job done.
beats.got: Start from the teammate's job, not from my tool.

beats.trigger: does it name one teammate, their current way of doing the job, and an outcome you could observe?
beats.got: A concrete test for whether the agent's job-to-be-done write-up is specific enough. I can apply it straight away.

beats.trigger: If the reason is merely *"we already have the platform,"* send it back.
beats.got: I have to justify the sharing form by the outcome, not by what tooling we own.

beats.trigger: You now have the teammate's job and a candidate selected against it.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: find the obstacle that decides whether the teammate can actually absorb it
beats.got: Next step is finding the real obstacle, then planning around it.

beats.trigger: A good bottleneck explains why several other obstacles stay hard.
beats.got: Look for the one blocker that makes the others hard, not the first limitation I notice. That is how I'd brief my CFO.

beats.trigger: A polished technical file beside a people file full of unnamed roles is the finding, not a finished rollout.
beats.got: My team will have a polished tech plan and empty owner slots, and that gap is what I should look at.

beats.trigger: checks the assumptions underneath these plans
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The technical and people plans are hypotheses.
beats.got: Treat the plans as hypotheses to test.

beats.trigger: what would have to be true for this teammate, doing this job, to fire their current hire and use my candidate?
beats.got: A sharp question that makes me compare against what Mikael does today. It's a bit consultant-y, but it works.

beats.trigger: one person, one question about how they do the job today, and one selected assumption with its test.
beats.got: Monday becomes one named conversation and one test, which is small enough that I'd do it.

beats.trigger: Test the switch, not the solution.
beats.got: A summary of what I just did.

beats.trigger: The rest of this is about the person on the other end of your plan.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: A candidate that does not move it is not a candidate.
beats.got: Same point as the exercise intro. The 'third outcome' idea (an anxiety gone, a dependency removed) is mildly interesting.

beats.trigger: Hand someone the agent file and they run it, get a generic answer, and quietly stop.
beats.got: If I forward my pricing-brief setup, my team will get weak output and drop it. The value is in my curated sources and corrections.

beats.trigger: Accountability is the part with a name on it, and a name does not travel inside a folder.
beats.got: Context, boundary and checks copy easily. Who answers for the output doesn't, and I'm that person for my team.

beats.trigger: The interface is the first piece whose shape depends on somebody whose calendar you do not control.
beats.got: Not sure what it adds. It sounds like a transition line.

beats.trigger: The leadership had not done the analysis. People they trusted had.
beats.got: Even a good agent-built proposal died because the deciders hadn't done the work themselves. That could happen to my pricing decision with the CFO.

beats.trigger: The two get reported as one number and they are not one thing.
beats.got: Rollout counts say nothing about adoption. Fair, and I recognise it from our licence reports.

beats.trigger: *we know more than we can tell.*
beats.got: People need something familiar to attach a new thing to. Polanyi is a bit academic, and I'd have got there without him.

beats.trigger: Somebody they trust has to have used it first and said so.
beats.got: nothing new. This repeats the switch question from the exercise. The trusted-peer point is the one useful bit.

beats.trigger: What you learned getting here is not one of the four things.
beats.got: nothing new. It's a restatement, and the last line is vague.

beats.trigger: One person whose week this would change, who would tell you plainly if it did not.
beats.got: A missing name is a finding, and I should find one person who'd be honest with me.

beats.trigger: The agent reviews, rewrites the sharing artifact in place, and reports what changed.
beats.got: Housekeeping: the agent cleans up my sharing file. Fine, as long as it edits only the section I flag.

beats.trigger: plus one line in your Module 7 next-step file naming the first move.
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: Access is easy; absorption is scarce.
beats.got: nothing new, just the summary

beats.trigger: Test one assumption. Ask for one name. Talk to one person.
beats.got: I have homework before the next module, and it's the same small move as Monday.

beats.trigger: What comes back from that contact is Module 8's raw material.
beats.got: nothing new

take_homes: Don't hand my team my agent setup, because it will give them generic output. What carries is the curated context and sources, so that is what I put in one shared place.
Fill the people plan names first. An empty owner slot is the real gap, and I need to be the named person who answers for the output.
Before I roll anything out, ask one teammate how they do the job today and what would make them drop that for my version.

monday.move: Take the pilot-cohort brief setup and turn it into a shared context folder (sources, style notes, my corrections). Then ask Mikael how he builds the pricing summary today and what would make him switch.
monday.who: Mikael on the pricing working group, then the other thirteen once he's tried it
monday.when: Monday morning for the interview, then a first test with Mikael by Wednesday
monday.stop_condition: If Mikael's output from the shared folder is no better than what he does now, I stop and rethink the form. I don't roll it out to the others.
monday.blocker: We have no shared place for the context files, so I need IT to give me a team folder. I also need to decide who owns the sources once I'm not the only one editing.

misconception.why: The module says the value is in the curated memory, corrections and judgement, not in the instruction file. That is hard to square with 'better prompts', but nothing here showed me how good I'd have to get at the rest, so I still half believe it.

one_line: Good for making you put names on your rollout plan, and the failed-workshop story hits hard, but the lecture says the access-versus-absorption point about four times.
